<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD follows standard packaging practices. The source is a pinned tag tarball fetched from the project's own upstream GitHub repository (github.com/multikernel/kerf), matching the declared url, and a SHA256 checksum is provided (not SKIP). The build() function runs the standard Python build toolchain (`python -m build --wheel`), and package() installs the resulting wheel with `python -m installer` into `$pkgdir` — both are routine operations. The `strip` command only targets a file inside the package's own site-packages data directory (`kerf/data/kerf-init`), which is a legitimate packaging step for a bundled static musl binary that makepkg's default strip logic misses. The `--no-isolation` flag is a minor hygiene note (build backend comes from makedepends rather than an isolated env) but is not malicious. No network requests to unrelated hosts, no obfuscated/encoded commands, no eval/curl|bash, no exfiltration, and no modifications outside the package scope were found.
</details>
